generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1; unique per table; never NULL. Parent PK sets are dense (1..n) so child multiplicities are constructible.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Drawn only from the FINAL parent primary-key set after PK generation; never NULL; child_count per distinct parent value is constructed to yield group sizes 1, 2 and >= 3 where the spec requires it; at least one parent row is left without children for each FK relationship.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random token of 3-12 lowercase letters; near-variants (case/whitespace/one-char edits) for any listed literal.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_email: Random local part + '@example.' + {com,org,net}; a '%wrau%' literal is included whenever Staff.email_address is generated with literals.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_phone: Random digits with optional separators, length 10-15.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_address: Random number + capitalized word + street suffix.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_city: Random capitalized word + suffix (port, berg, haven, bury, ville, stad).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_state: Uniform from a fixed list of US state names.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_code: Uniform from the enum listed in per_column_exceptions.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Uniform random datetime between 1970-01-01 and 2015-12-31, formatted 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_price: Uniform random decimal in [0.01, 200.00] rounded to 4 places; the sampler pool for a decimal column is filtered to numeric values only (non-numeric literals are never routed to numeric/decimal columns).
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, plant NULLs with share max(observed compact share, a small planted share of 10%) and force at least one NULL row per nullable column per instance whenever row count >= 1; NULLs are planted LAST, after duplicate/tie/group-size/boundary post-processing; a planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule or formula; NOT NULL and primary-key columns never receive NULL. Nullable detection must be by the schema's NOT NULL flag, not by pk_pos.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary: For numeric columns with a listed literal, include the literal, literal-1 step, literal+1 step.
generic_sampling_rules.tie: For ORDER columns, ensure at least two rows share the value at the listed rank; ties must survive any subsequent group-size or PK reindexing step; run tie injection AFTER group-size post-processing for columns that also carry group_sizes.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate: For DISTINCT columns, ensure 20-50% of values are duplicates of another row's value. Never apply this rule to a primary-key or UNIQUE column.
generic_sampling_rules.literal_routing: String literals are never routed to numeric/decimal columns; numeric columns accept only numeric literals. Literal pools are seeded per column from the listed literal_pool_other_columns only (the three literals in this specification); pool SQL extraction does not widen the pool.
generic_sampling_rules.table_size_authority: table_sizes_per_instance is authoritative: the program must pass these sizes to build_random_instance (not None). Each table's size is at least the minimum required by its group_sizes (6) and tie (2) targets.

issues.title: Price sampler draws non-numeric values, crashing 14/20 instances
issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 14 of 20 units fail with ValueError("could not convert string to float: 'Chocolate'") at tscore_gen/instance.py:80 (`cols['product_price'] = [None if v is None else max(0.0, float(v)) ...]`). Root cause: in values.py `make_spec_sampler`, the `'price' in column.name.lower() or 'decimal' in t` branch builds `els = list(ov) + pool` where `pool` contains string literals routed from queries (e.g. 'Chocolate' from a product_name literal that the loose FK-root routing in literals.py assigned to Products.product_price). PriceSampler then returns `r.choice(self.elements)` (a string) with probability `1-p`, so non-numeric strings reach `_enforce_semantic_rules`. The specification's `decimal_price` rule (uniform decimal in [0.01, 200.00]) is therefore not implemented for the sampled values.
issues.requested_revision: In `make_spec_sampler` (or `PriceSampler`), filter the element pool to numeric values only (drop non-numeric strings) before constructing the sampler, and/or coerce/validate in `_enforce_semantic_rules` so a non-numeric value cannot reach `float()`. Ensure every generated `product_price` is a decimal in [0.01, 200.00] as the specification requires. Re-run generation and confirm n_fail == 0.

issues.title: Foreign-key violations in 4 of 6 written instances (159 FK violations)
issues.evidence: Execution feedback: `fk_violations: 159`; per-instance `new_fk_violations` of 41, 55, 44, 19 on Complaints.product_id, Complaints.staff_id, Complaints.customer_id. The `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` function draws child FK values from `compact_parent` + `instance[pt][pc]`, but the parent's generated PKs are subsequently filtered by `sample_fresh_primary_keys` (and `drop_unique_duplicates`), so child rows can reference parent keys that were dropped. Also, `UNMATCHED_PARENT` post-processing drops child rows but does not re-validate that remaining child FKs still exist. The specification's `dependencies` (Complaints.staff_id -> Staff.staff_id, Complaints.product_id -> Products.product_id, Complaints.customer_id -> Customers.customer_id) are not enforced.
issues.requested_revision: Generate parent PKs first, then draw child FKs only from the *final* parent PK set (after fresh-PK filtering and unique-dropping). Re-validate all child FKs after the UNMATCHED_PARENT step and drop or re-point any orphaned child rows. Confirm `fk_violations == 0` in the execution feedback.

issues.title: NULL rule not applied to most nullable columns
issues.evidence: Execution feedback `nullable_columns` shows `NULL 0 / n` for Customers.address_line_1/2, email_address, phone_number, state, town_city; Products.parent_product_id, product_description, product_name; Staff.first_name, gender, last_name, phone_number. The specification's `null_targets` lists all of these and the interface rule requires at least one NULL row per nullable column. In `build_random_instance`, `apply_null_rule` is called with `nullable = not cm.notnull and cm.pk_pos == 0`; for these columns the sampler's `max_l0` cap and the `apply_duplicate_share`/`apply_tie`/`apply_group_sizes` post-processing run *after* the NULL rule and overwrite the planted NULLs (e.g. `apply_duplicate_share` copies a non-NULL source value into a NULL slot; `apply_tie`/`apply_group_sizes` overwrite indices). The interface rule states a planted NULL is never replaced.
issues.requested_revision: Apply the NULL rule last (after duplicate/tie/group-size/boundary post-processing), or make those post-processors skip NULL slots. Ensure each nullable column has at least one NULL and a share matching the compact database's share. Re-run and confirm the `nullable_columns` lines show NULL > 0 for every listed column.

issues.title: Literal routing assigns unrelated string literals to numeric columns
issues.evidence: The crash 'Chocolate' reaching Products.product_price shows that `seed_literal_pool_from_queries` (loose=True) routes a product_name literal to the FK-root of product_price. The specification's `literal_pool_other_columns` lists only `Complaints.complaint_type_code: ['Product Failure']`, `Customers.customer_type_code: ['Good Credit Rating']`, `Staff.email_address: ['%wrau%']`, but the pool actually contains 'Chocolate' for a price column. The specification does not describe this routing behavior or constrain which literals may reach which columns.

This is a specification gap that the engineer's fix must be consistent with.

issues.issue: The NULL rule is specified but never actually applied to generated instances: every nullable column shows 'generated rows: NULL 0 / n' in the execution feedback, for all 20 instances.
issues.evidence: nullable_columns feedback lists 'generated rows: NULL 0 / 399' (Complaints), 'NULL 0 / 144' (Customers), 'NULL 0 / 175' (Products), 'NULL 0 / 178' (Staff) for every column. In values.py, apply_null_rule() computes k = round(n * null_share) and forces k>=1, so at least one NULL should be planted whenever the column is nullable and n>=1. In instance.py the call is apply_null_rule(inst[t][cm.name], rng, schema.null_share.get(key, 0.0), True). apply_null_rule's signature is (values, rng, null_share, nullable) and it does plant NULLs when nullable=True. But then the writer writes rows: `n = len(cols.get(names[0], []))` and `rows.append([cols[c][i] for c in names])`. That is not the bug. The bug is that build_random_instance runs `_revalidate_fks(inst, schema, schema.fks)` BEFORE the NULL loop (so NULLs for FK columns still work), but the NULL loop is applied to `inst[t][cm.name]`. That is fine. However, `apply_null_rule` uses `nullable = (not cm.notnull) and cm.pk_pos == 0`. That is true for nullable columns. So NULLs should appear. Re-read: apply_null_rule shuffles indices and sets values[i]=None. That should work. Unless build_random_instance stores values in `cols` dict and then does `inst[t][cm.name] = apply_null_rule(inst[t][cm.name], rng, schema.null_share.get(key, 0.0), True)`. That reassigns. So NULLs would be planted. Yet the execution feedback shows 0 NULLs. Possible cause: the reported execution of the program run is against the specification's NULL handling — but the feedback says the run added 0 NULLs. This is a contradiction with the code. Either the reported feedback is from an older run or the code path differs. Regardless, the observable outcome is 0 NULLs on all nullable columns across 20 instances, which violates interface rule 7 ('each instance contains generated rows with NULL ... and at least one NULL row per nullable column').
issues.requested_revision: Investigate why no NULLs appear despite apply_null_rule forcing k>=1; reproduce on one instance and confirm at least one NULL per nullable column per instance, matching the compact NULL share (planted small share).

issues.issue: The literal_routing / numeric-only filtering is specified (string literals must not reach numeric columns; numeric literals only reach numeric columns), and the program claims to implement it in seed_literal_pool_from_queries via `anc = [a for a in anc if _is_numeric_col(a) == vn]`. This is consistent with the spec. But the spec also says 'Literal pools are seeded per column from the listed literal_pool_other_columns only' (generic_sampling_rules.literal_routing). The code seeds from all extracted literals in the pool SQLs, not just the three listed literals.
issues.evidence: specification.json generic_sampling_rules.literal_routing: 'Literal pools are seeded per column from the listed literal_pool_other_columns only.' literal_pool_other_columns lists only 3 literals: Complaints.complaint_type_code='Product Failure', Customers.customer_type_code='Good Credit Rating', Staff.email_address='%wrau%'. But seed_literal_pool_from_queries extracts values from 230 pool SQLs (pool_sqls=230, pool_values=65) and routes all of them, producing a pool much larger than the three spec literals.
issues.requested_revision: Either restrict literal seeding to the three listed literal_pool_other_columns, or amend the specification to allow seeding from the pool SQLs (and drop the 'only' clause). Choose one; they must be consistent.

issues.issue: Several specified patterns have insufficient evidence / ambiguous targets that the program cannot reliably satisfy.
issues.evidence:
(a) Customers.customer_id has both a 'duplicates_for_distinct' target (20-50%) and a 'group_sizes' target (1,2,>=3) and a 'ties_for_order_limit' target. customer_id is a PRIMARY KEY: 20-50% duplicate share is impossible for a PK. The program's apply_duplicate_share would break the PK (with 8 rows, 20-50% duplicates means ~2 duplicates), which is then filtered by sample_fresh_primary_keys — so the DISTINCT target on a PK is unsatisfiable by construction. Similar conflict for Products.product_id (PK with group_sizes + tie targets). The spec lists Customers.customer_id duplicates_for_distinct; this is an unsatisfiable pattern on a PK.
(b) apply_group_sizes requires n>=6 (returns unchanged otherwise) but is specified on Products (n=4) and Staff (n=7). With table_sizes_per_instance Products=4, the group-sizes target on Products.product_id / product_name / parent_product_id cannot be met. The spec says table sizes per instance Products=4; group_sizes requires sizes 1,2,>=3 which needs at least 6 rows. Unsatisfiable.
(c) Products.product_price rows_with_different_values requires >=2 distinct values; the code fixes that with `vals[0]=0.01; vals[1]=200.0`. But the VALUES sampler PriceSampler caps at [0.01,200.00]. With n=4 satisfying >=2 distinct is fine, but the (a) and (b) conflicts remain.
issues.requested_revision: Remove or restate the unsatisfiable patterns: drop duplicates_for_distinct on primary-key columns (Customers.customer_id, Products.product_id, Staff.staff_id) since PKs cannot have duplicate shares; and increase the per-instance table size for Products (or drop the group_sizes target on Products) so group sizes 1,2,>=3 can exist. Do this in the specification, not per query.

issues.issue: Tie targets at rank 1 for COUNT(*) on group columns are not verified: tie injection in apply_tie sets two rows to the same value, but 'tie_at_rank [1] direction ASC and DESC tie_on COUNT(*)' requires that the top-1 and top-1-desc group sizes are tied (i.e., two values share the smallest COUNT(*) and two share the largest COUNT(*)). apply_tie on the raw column values does not control group counts — it duplicates a cell value, which changes a group count. This is roughly aligned, but for numeric PKs apply_group_sizes overwrites nn[0..5] AFTER apply_tie, potentially destroying the tie.
issues.evidence: values.py apply_group_sizes sets values[nn[0..5]] to sentinels g1, g2, g2, g3, g3, g3 — so at minimum groups of size 1, 2, 3 exist. But if apply_tie ran before, its tie may be among earlier indices and get overwritten by group_sizes (since nn was shuffled inside group_sizes but not coordinatied with tie). Order in instance.py is: duplicate -> tie -> group_sizes. group_sizes' shuffle can overwrite the duplicated pair, breaking the tie-at-rank target. No post-check confirms ties survive.
issues.requested_revision: Reorder so apply_tie runs AFTER apply_group_sizes (or have apply_group_sizes preserve existing ties), then verify that the specified rank has the required tie in each instance.

issues.evidence: instance.py _revalidate_fks: when invalid FKs exist it re-points them to sorted(pset)[0] AND then does 'rows[ct] = _filter(rows[ct], keep)' where keep excludes the invalid rows — so the re-pointed values are discarded and rows are dropped anyway. The docstring claims 'Rows needed for group_sizes/tie targets are never dropped', but the code drops them. Also the UNMATCHED_PARENT block drops child rows referencing the last parent, which can reduce Complaints below its size target and break FK/group-size targets.
issues.requested_revision: Make _revalidate_fks consistent with its stated contract: either re-point without dropping, or drop without claiming preservation. Ensure the unmatched-parent step does not reduce a child table below its group_sizes/tie minimum (e.g. only drop when child count exceeds the minimum).

issues.evidence: instance.py fill_foreign_keys_consistently draws FK values uniformly at random from the parent set; there is no construction of child_count per parent to yield group sizes 1, 2 and >=3 as the spec's integer_fk rule requires ('child_count per distinct parent value is constructed to yield group sizes 1, 2 and >= 3 where the spec requires it'). The spec retains group_sizes on Products.product_id via Complaints.product_id FK distribution (uncertainty note), but the program does not construct this distribution.
issues.requested_revision: Construct Complaints.product_id multiplicities explicitly so that per-parent child counts include 1, 2 and >=3 (and leave >=1 parent without children), rather than uniform random draws. This is required for the retained group_sizes target on Products.product_id.

issues.evidence: values.py GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS = {('Products','product_name'), ('Products','parent_product_id')} — it omits ('Products','product_id'), which the spec retains via the Complaints FK distribution. Also GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS includes ('Products','parent_product_id'), a nullable self-FK; apply_group_sizes writes sentinel strings 'g1_...' into a numeric INTEGER column when numeric=False is passed (instance.py passes numeric=_is_numeric_col(cm), so this is avoided for parent_product_id — but the spec's group_sizes on parent_product_id is not clearly satisfiable given NULL planting last).
issues.requested_revision: Align GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS with the spec's retained targets and document how parent_product_id group sizes survive NULL planting (NULLs are planted last and may destroy the 1/2/>=3 distribution). Either exclude parent_product_id from GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS or re-verify group sizes after NULL planting.

issues.evidence: Spec's uncertainty note claims 'group_sizes 1,2,>=3 on product_name and parent_product_id are satisfiable' with Products size 6, but NULL planting is applied last and forces >=1 NULL per nullable column. With 6 rows and >=1 NULL, only 5 non-NULL values remain, which cannot realize group sizes 1,2,>=3 (needs >=6 non-NULL rows). The spec is internally inconsistent for parent_product_id.
issues.requested_revision: Either raise Products table size to >=7 (so 6 non-NULL rows remain after NULL planting) or drop the group_sizes target on parent_product_id. Update table_sizes_per_instance accordingly.

issues.evidence: Spec's semantic_rules_and_formulas lists 'Products.date_product_discontinued >= date_product_first_available' as a rule with evidence 'NOT ENFORCED ... contradictory rows remain allowed'. A rule that is explicitly not enforced and whose evidence contradicts it is not a supported rule; it should be classified as an uncertain/unsupported pattern rather than a semantic rule.
issues.requested_revision: Move the discontinued-vs-first-available ordering out of semantic_rules_and_formulas into an explicit 'unsupported/uncertain patterns' section, or remove it. Keep only rules with positive evidence (product_price >= 0; complaint closed >= raised).

issues.evidence: values.py apply_tie for direction 'BOTH' sets values[other] = values[best] where best is the min and other is the max — this collapses the max to the min, destroying the DESC-side tie and potentially the ASC-side ordering. The spec requires tie_at_rank [1] for both ASC and DESC on product_price, product_id, product_name.
issues.requested_revision: Implement BOTH as two independent ties: ensure >=2 rows share the minimum value AND >=2 rows share the maximum value (without overwriting the max with the min).

issues.evidence: values.py apply_duplicate_share: 'target = int(round(n * rng.uniform(0.2,0.5)))' then 'target = max(1, min(target, len(nn)-1))'. For small n (e.g. Customers size 8, ~31 generated rows observed) the duplicate share may fall outside 20-50% of total rows because NULLs are excluded from nn and the cap uses len(nn)-1. The spec requires 20-50% of values to be duplicates.
issues.requested_revision: Compute the duplicate count against total row count n (not just non-NULL count) and verify the resulting duplicate share is within [0.2, 0.5] of n; document how NULLs interact with the share.

issues.evidence: instance.py _enforce_semantic_rules clamps product_price to [0.01, 200.0] and fixes complaint dates, but the spec's DIFFERENT_VALUE_COLUMNS handling in instance.py sets vals[0]=0.01, vals[1]=200.0 only when <2 distinct non-NULL values exist — this runs BEFORE _enforce_semantic_rules and before NULL planting, so the MAX/MIN scalar subquery target (>=2 different values per group) may be broken by NULL planting or clamping. Also the spec's rows_with_different_values target is '>= 2 per group with different values' — the program only ensures 2 distinct values overall, not per group.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure >=2 distinct non-NULL product_price values survive NULL planting and clamping, and clarify whether 'per group' means per product category or overall; implement accordingly.

issues.evidence: cli.py _spec_pool seeds pool only for keys present in schema.original_values ('if key not in schema.original_values: continue'). If a literal's column has no compact rows (or key mismatch), the literal is silently dropped. Execution feedback shows pool_values 3 (all three literals seeded), so this specific case works, but the guard is fragile.
issues.requested_revision: Seed the pool regardless of whether the column has compact values (the literal should still be routed to its named column), or log a warning when a spec literal is dropped.

issues.evidence: instance.py sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates run AFTER per-column sampling and post-processing (duplicate/group/tie), so PK/unique filtering can drop rows and reduce table size below the spec's authoritative size (e.g. Products 6, Complaints 12). Execution feedback shows rows_added per instance as low as 3-9 total across all tables (e.g. unit 0017 rows_added 3), far below the sum of spec sizes (7+8+6+12=33), indicating heavy row dropping.
issues.requested_revision: Generate PKs/unique values first (or regenerate dropped rows) so the final appended row count per table meets table_sizes_per_instance. The spec states table_sizes_per_instance is authoritative and must be passed to build_random_instance; the program passes it but does not guarantee the resulting row counts.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback 'construction_pairs': eligible 52, separated 14 — only 14 of 52 eligible pairs separated. While the instructions note a missing separation alone does not prove an error, combined with the NULL 0/n evidence and row-dropping, the low separation rate is consistent with targets not being realized.
issues.requested_revision: After fixing NULL planting and row-dropping, re-run and report separation; investigate pairs that remain unseparated to confirm targets (duplicates, ties, group sizes, boundaries) are actually constructed.

Whether the writer's INSERT INTO t VALUES (...) with all columns preserves NULLs (it should, but the 0/NULL evidence contradicts the invariant).

Whether the 'BOTH' tie direction is correctly implemented for product_price/product_id/product_name.

Whether table_sizes_per_instance row counts are actually met after PK/unique filtering and FK revalidation.
